questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It seemed attractive as it has been listed as one of the best universities of life science in europe. Additionally, I was super impressed by the pictures of campus and I must say that it definitely met my expectations. The study life in Wageningen was also one if the criteria of why I chose this city. It's a small city where you easily get to know a lot of people and there are a lot of opportunities to be social. The sporting facilities are also really good, they have a huge sports area with both inside and outside facilities and as an exchange student you can get a nice offer of membership.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Going abroad in Wageningen was really a nice experience. I got to meet a lot of amazing people and got new friendships across the world. Going to the Netherlands is also a nice opportunity to travel in the country but also to other european countries as traveling with train and bus is super easy and cheap. For instance I went to Brussels, Berlin, Paris and Barcelona with people who now are some of my best friends and who I still have weekly contact to after coming back to DK.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really easy. Wageningen university send a lot of information to you when you get accepted, and if you need additional information, the exchange coordinators are really nice to help you and answer you pretty fast.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I joined the AID program where I got my to amazing mentors who were always happy to answer any question you should have.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of options for housing on campus. I lived in the Bornsesteeg building which was only 5min by walking to campus. Wageningen is a small city, so when you live off campus it is basically on campus as it is only 15min by bike from campus

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in a self-contained room so I had my own kitchen and then I shared fridge and freezer with my corridor. Most people in my corridor had their own fridge, so there was a lot of free space in the common fridge that I used.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: When you get offered a room just accept it as Wageningen is a small city where you will never live far from campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was online on Osiris. The exchange coordinators can always answer your questions and help you

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinators and spot on events on going abroad

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: If you just apply before the deadline you normally get enrolled in the courses you wish to follow

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Expect to study much more than you do at KU. The courses are really interesting and the professors super nice, but all the exams are closed book exams, so you really need to study a lot.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All of the courses had a really nice level, easy to follow and the study load was okay. All courses except from Plant Biotechnology had an exam level complementary to the level of the course. The Plant Biotechnology exam had a really high level and the content of the exam didn't meet the content of the study material and the lectures.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had much more group work at WUR compared to UCPH, but other than that it was quite similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Introduction to law for the life sciences
2. Introduction to bioinformatics
3. Plant biotechnology
4. Genomics
5. Enzymology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Introduction to law for the life sciences was super interesting as it gave a different perspective on life science.
Additionally, I also like Genomics a lot and the professors in this course were really helpful

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: As my room was self-cointed I had to spend money on all kitchen equipments, a vacuum cleaner and so forth.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport was more expensive than expected, it was more expensive than it is in DK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There was the Buddy program where you get your buddy family. A lot of activities are organized by the ESN, among those laser tag, karaoke night, different cultural kitchens.
There are really nice sporting facilities too.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: AID and buddy program

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: travel, party at the International club, go to the market (which is there every Wednesday and Saturday)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. There not really big cultural differences between Denmark and the Netherlands

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There's a lot of group work where you get to meet a lot of local students. Otherwise, you can just meet them at the parties

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were not really any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their kindness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- be open-minded
- Join the AID
- get yourself a bike and explore the nature of Wageningen

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friendships I got

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the administrative work you had to do on arrival

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
